problem.statement: BThwani needs one governed financial capability that preserves WLT-owned internal wallet truth while safely connecting official-wallet Cash-In, captain COD exposure, stakeholder earnings and manually executed external settlements without duplicate money movement, parallel ledgers, unverifiable completion or dependence on spreadsheets/operator memory.
problem.currentWorkaround: The current implementation contains strong WLT ledger and finance boundaries but still mixes legacy provider-managed payout states, bank/manual destination semantics, COD collect/remit behavior, partial top-up/payment allocation support and separate finance inspectors; the target rules are currently concentrated in a service architecture document rather than one capability Product Truth.

actors.role: Customer funding or paying through supported WLT-governed payment paths and reading only their own internal financial state.
permittedActions: read own internal wallet and ledger references
forbiddenActions: assert top-up success
directly mutate wallet balance
select provider credentials
withdraw internal balance unless a separately approved capability permits it

actors.role: Captain using one WLT internal wallet for approved funding, order-specific COD financial exposure, earnings and governed settlement requests.
permittedActions: receive governed delivery or commission earnings
request eligible settlement to a verified destination
forbiddenActions: accept COD exposure not atomically covered by the governed wallet rule
mutate COD reserve or balance locally
treat future earnings as existing COD capacity
assume the visible balance is fully withdrawable
complete external settlement locally

actors.role: Partner receiving WLT-calculated governed proceeds and requesting settlement to an approved official-wallet destination.
permittedActions: read own wallet and settlement references
submit or maintain destination information for verification
forbiddenActions: select an arbitrary unsupported external provider
activate an unverified destination
edit an approved payout snapshot
mark settlement paid

actors.role: Field actor receiving only governed earned commissions and requesting eligible settlement to a verified official-wallet destination.
forbiddenActions: self-create commission value
activate an unverified destination
request more than server-owned withdrawal eligibility
complete external settlement

actors.role: Permission-scoped operator preparing, approving, executing, verifying, reconciling and closing financial work only through the assigned governed role transitions.
permittedActions: prepare or review payout according to role
record required execution reference and evidence
close a business date only when gates pass
forbiddenActions: directly edit wallet or ledger balances
change approved beneficiary destination or amount in place
use a bare mark-paid transition
silently bypass separation of duties
treat XLSX or screenshot as financial truth
close blocking unresolved exposure

actors.role: WLT-owned financial engine, provider adapters, reconciliation and policy enforcement producing canonical ledger and audit truth.
permittedActions: reserve release and finalize governed COD exposure
enforce idempotency and legal state transitions
forbiddenActions: route an ambiguous money mutation to a second provider before the first outcome is authoritative
credit from client claims or screenshots
use mock or sandbox as production fallback
create parallel provider or stakeholder ledgers
silently mutate historical financial evidence

routesOrScreens: WLT wallet ledger payment COD payout settlement provider and reconciliation owners
WLT canonical ledger and wallet tables
actions: prevent in-place mutation of approved or frozen financial facts

routesOrScreens: generated financial contracts and shared presentation adapters

outcome.statement: Every BThwani money movement is attributable to one WLT-owned wallet/ledger truth and, where external money moves, to one authoritative provider or manual-settlement evidence chain from intent through reconciliation and close, with no parallel wallet, spreadsheet, provider or frontend truth.
outcome.primaryMetric: share of financial movements with complete WLT ledger lineage and required external evidence/reconciliation lineage
outcome.baselineState: Canonical ledger and finance ownership exist, but important target Cash-In, COD allocation and manual external settlement controls are only partially implemented and some legacy provider-payout/COD semantics remain.
outcome.targetState: Cash-In, order allocation, captain COD, stakeholder earnings, verified destinations, manual settlement batches, evidence, reconciliation and financial close all use one WLT-owned governed state machine and evidence chain.
outcome.observationWindow: targeted static, contract, migration, concurrency, runtime simulator, cross-surface, finance-control, security and reconciliation verification on the same candidate

criteria: WLT remains the sole writer of internal wallet balances, ledger transactions, payments, refunds, commissions, payouts, settlements and reconciliation truth.
Each actor has one canonical internal WLT wallet; held, pending, earned, settled and withdrawal-eligibility values are states/projections and do not create parallel wallets or ledgers.
Cash-In credits an internal wallet only after authoritative provider evidence is verified/normalized and the server-owned financial purpose selects the accounting destination.
Mock/sandbox provider behavior is retained for non-production testing but cannot be selected as a production fallback.
Every applicable order has one server-owned PaymentAllocation whose components conserve the governed order total and make delivery-fee treatment mechanically non-duplicative.
Captain COD authorization is order-specific and atomic; concurrent assignments cannot consume the same available balance, cancellation releases once, and finalization debits once.

The target captain-funded COD path cannot simultaneously create a second remittance liability for the same order value; any alternate custody/remittance model requires an explicit Product Truth and cannot coexist for the same financial effect.

One visible wallet balance does not imply full withdrawal eligibility; customer withdrawal and externally funded principal cash-out remain disabled unless an explicitly approved product/legal-financial policy enables them.
Partner, captain and field payouts use one WLT-owned payout engine with stakeholder-specific eligibility expressed as policy rather than separate ledgers.
Only a verified active version of an official-wallet destination can be used for settlement, and a destination identifier change requires re-verification.
Approval binds beneficiary, destination version, amount, currency and policy context to an immutable snapshot; a material change cannot edit the approved snapshot in place.
Approved payouts are grouped into immutable frozen settlement batches with exact row count/control total and integrity metadata; XLSX/export remains an audited execution artifact only.
Manual external execution records the required external reference and evidence and cannot expose a bare mark-paid transition.

Final payout completion requires the Product Truth-mandated agreement between approved payout, frozen batch row, execution evidence and authoritative external statement/record; mismatch creates a blocking reconciliation exception.

Financial separation of duties is enforced server-side for preparation, approval, execution, independent verification/reconciliation and close according to active policy; exceptions are explicit, bounded and audited.
Blocking finance exceptions, missing required evidence, control-total mismatch or unresolved material reconciliation exposure prevent affected payout/batch/day completion.
Refund routing follows the authoritative original money source and does not silently convert external refunds to internal balance unless explicit product policy allows it.
An ambiguous external mutation result is reconciled before any new provider/route attempt can move the same money again.
External official-wallet account balances are reconciled as treasury/control facts without becoming a second internal wallet ledger.

All sensitive destination identifiers, external references, exports and financial audit data follow encryption, masking, least-privilege, integrity and retention rules from the active security policy.
requiredChecks: captain COD concurrency and idempotency tests
Cash-In provider-event replay and unknown-result tests

business: WLT is the sole internal financial truth owner and every value-changing movement is represented by the canonical double-entry ledger.
Official external wallets move external money but do not own internal BThwani balances, liabilities or settlement state.
There is one internal wallet per actor and one canonical payout engine for partner, captain and field.
Order payment composition and COD exposure are server-owned financial facts, not UI/provider labels.
The current production Cash-Out model is governed manual external official-wallet settlement; automated payout requires a separately approved capability.
Financial completion requires the evidence and reconciliation chain declared by the capability, not merely operator intent.
Unknown or conflicting external outcomes remain reconcilable until authoritative evidence resolves them.
negative: No DSH or frontend component writes WLT balances or ledger truth.
No provider name determines the internal ledger account or stakeholder entitlement.
No client screenshot, operator claim, spreadsheet edit or unverified file row creates financial success.
No unverified or silently changed official-wallet destination receives payout.
No frozen batch or approved payout snapshot is edited in place.
No required finance control silently disappears because a production environment variable is absent.
No second provider is invoked for the same ambiguous external mutation before reconciliation.
No legacy COD custody/remit path and captain-wallet debit path both account for the same order value.
No daily financial close hides unresolved blocking exposure or mismatched control totals.

execution.appetite: Consolidate all real-money and internal-money financial effects into one WLT-owned, evidence-backed and reconcilable capability while preserving non-production simulator value and removing legacy parallel payout/COD semantics only after affected consumers are migrated.
fixedConstraints: manual governed external settlement as current Cash-Out model
immutable approved payout and frozen batch facts
variableScope: which approved Cash-In provider is active
destination verification method supported by operations
forbiddenScope: provider-managed automated payout as current default
bank/IBAN as the target stakeholder settlement model
production deployment or provider activation without separate authorization
unknowns: exact production Cash-In provider private contract and API semantics
exact approved operational method for destination verification
final product/legal policy for withdrawal eligibility of externally funded principal
final governed treatment of delivery cash versus separate WLT delivery earning
future availability and approval of automated payout capabilities
